title: 412. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: State the cosecant of an acute angle as a ratio of sides of a right triangle.
questions.question: In a right triangle with acute angle \(\theta\), which ratio equals \(\csc\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The cosecant is the reciprocal of the sine. Since \(\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\), \(\csc\theta=\frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{opposite}}\). The ratio \(\frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{adjacent}}\) is \(\sec\theta\), the reciprocal of the cosine.
questions.hint: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine; invert the sine ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a cosecant as the reciprocal of a given sine.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}\). What is \(\csc\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The cosecant is the reciprocal of the sine: \(\csc\theta=\frac{1}{\sin\theta}=\frac{5}{3}\). The value \(\frac{5}{4}\) is \(\sec\theta\), since \(\cos\theta=\frac{4}{5}\) for this angle.
questions.hint: Take the reciprocal of the given ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a secant as the reciprocal of a given cosine.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\cos\theta=\frac{5}{13}\). What is \(\sec\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The secant is the reciprocal of the cosine: \(\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=\frac{13}{5}\). The value \(\frac{13}{12}\) is \(\csc\theta\), since \(\sin\theta=\frac{12}{13}\) for this angle.
questions.hint: Secant pairs with cosine; invert the given fraction.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a cotangent as the reciprocal of a given tangent.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\tan\theta=\frac{7}{24}\). What is \(\cot\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The cotangent is the reciprocal of the tangent: \(\cot\theta=\frac{1}{\tan\theta}=\frac{24}{7}\). The value \(\frac{24}{25}\) is \(\cos\theta\), obtained from the hypotenuse \(\sqrt{7^2+24^2}=25\).
questions.hint: Cotangent is the adjacent side over the opposite side.

questions.concept: Secant from the legs of a triangle
questions.learningObjective: Find the hypotenuse and then a secant ratio from two legs.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite an acute angle \(\theta\) is \(9\) and the side adjacent to \(\theta\) is \(12\). What is \(\sec\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{9^2+12^2}=\sqrt{225}=15\). Then \(\sec\theta=\frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{15}{12}=\frac{5}{4}\). The value \(\frac{5}{3}=\frac{15}{9}\) is \(\csc\theta\).
questions.hint: Find the hypotenuse first; secant uses the hypotenuse and the adjacent side.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a reciprocal ratio at a standard angle.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\csc 30^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\sin 30^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\), \(\csc 30^\circ=\frac{1}{\sin 30^\circ}=2\). The value \(\frac{1}{2}\) is the sine itself, not its reciprocal.
questions.hint: Find the sine of the angle first, then take its reciprocal.

questions.concept: Range of reciprocal ratios for acute angles
questions.learningObjective: Decide which values a reciprocal ratio of an acute angle can take.
questions.question: Which statement is impossible for an acute angle \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: For an acute angle, \(0<\cos\theta<1\), so \(\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}>1\); thus \(\sec\theta=0.8\) is impossible. The cotangent compares the two legs and can be any positive number; a triangle with adjacent side \(4\) and opposite side \(5\) gives \(\cot\theta=0.8\).
questions.hint: Think about the size of the cosine of an acute angle and what that implies for its reciprocal.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cotangent at a standard angle in simplified form.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\cot 60^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\tan 60^\circ=\sqrt{3}\), \(\cot 60^\circ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\). The value \(\sqrt{3}\) is \(\tan 60^\circ\) itself, which equals \(\cot 30^\circ\).
questions.hint: Take the reciprocal of \(\tan 60^\circ\) and rationalise the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Use a right triangle to convert one reciprocal ratio into another.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\csc\theta=\frac{13}{5}\). What is \(\cot\theta\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\csc\theta=\frac{\text{hypotenuse}}{\text{opposite}}\), take hypotenuse \(13\) and opposite side \(5\). The adjacent side is \(\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12\). Then \(\cot\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{opposite}}=\frac{12}{5}\). The value \(\frac{5}{12}\) is \(\tan\theta\).
questions.hint: Build a right triangle from the cosecant, find the missing leg, and then form adjacent over opposite.

questions.learningObjective: Use the relation between secant and tangent to find a tangent.
questions.question: For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\sec\theta=3\). What is \(\tan\theta\)?
questions.explanation: Take hypotenuse \(3\) and adjacent side \(1\). The opposite side is \(\sqrt{3^2-1^2}=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}\), so \(\tan\theta=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{1}=2\sqrt{2}\). Equivalently, \(\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta-1=8\). Adding instead of subtracting gives \(\sqrt{10}\), which is incorrect.
questions.hint: The hypotenuse is the longest side, so the missing leg comes from a difference of squares.
